Key Characteristics & Etiology: Bleeding from uterine corpus abnormal in duration/volume/frequency; etiology PALM-COEIN
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Structural (Polyps, Adenomyosis, Leiomyoma, Malignancy) or non-structural (Coagulopathy, Ovulatory, Endometrial, Iatrogenic)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Heavy flow, flooding, clots, fatigue, anemia; Red Flags: PMB, PCB, intermenstrual bleeding
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: FBC (ferritin); Pelvic TVUS; LNG-IUS (Mirena) 1st-line; Tranexamic acid / NSAIDs; Endometrial ablation / Hysterectomy

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Ectopic implantation of functional endometrial glands/stroma outside uterine cavity
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Retrograde menstruation / coelomic metaplasia with estrogen-dependent chronic inflammation
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: The 4 Ds: Dysmenorrhea, Deep Dyspareunia, Dyschezia, Dysuria; pelvic pain, subfertility; tender nodularity
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Pelvic TVUS (chocolate cysts); Laparoscopy + biopsy (Gold Standard); NSAIDs + COCP/Dienogest or Laparoscopic excision

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Benign invasion of endometrial tissue into uterine myometrium with smooth muscle hypertrophy
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Hyperplastic myometrium surrounding ectopic endometrial glands causing diffuse enlargement
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Secondary dysmenorrhea, heavy painful menses, enlarged tender globular/bogy uterus
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: TVUS (asymmetric myometrial thickening, myometrial cysts); MRI pelvis; LNG-IUS (Mirena) / Hysterectomy

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Primary: no menses by 15 with secondary sexual characteristics or 13 without; Secondary: absence >3-6 months
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis dysfunction, WHO Class I (hypogonadotropic), II (eugonadotropic/PCOS), III (hypergonadotropic/POF)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Lack of menses, galactorrhea, hirsutism, hot flashes; Red Flags: anosmia (Kallmann), visual loss (prolactinoma)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Pregnancy test (exclude pregnancy 1st); Serum FSH/LH, Prolactin, TSH, Testosterone; Progestin withdrawal test; Pelvic US

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Primary dysmenorrhea (excess prostaglandins without pathology) vs Secondary; PMS (luteal phase mood/somatic symptoms)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Prostaglandin F2-alpha induced myometrial hypercontractility & uterine ischemia; PMS progesterone sensitivity
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Painful cramping lower abdominal pain starting before/with menses; PMS: irritability, bloating, breast tenderness
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: NSAIDs (Mefenamic acid) started 1-2 days before menses; COCP; SSRIs for severe PMS/PMDD

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Proliferation of endometrial glands; Non-atypical vs Atypical (precancerous with 30% progression rate)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Unopposed estrogen stimulation (obesity, peripheral aromatization, PCOS, Tamoxifen, estrogen-only HRT)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Abnormal uterine bleeding, heavy irregular menses, Postmenopausal Bleeding (PMB - Red Flag)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: TVUS Endometrial Thickness (>4mm in PMB); Pipelle biopsy / Hysteroscopy & D&C; LNG-IUS for non-atypical; TH+BSO for atypical

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Includes Serous (70%), Mucinous, Endometrioid, Clear cell; BRCA1/2 and Lynch syndrome risk factors
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Incessant ovulation causing surface epithelial invagination & malignant genetic mutation
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Abdominal distension, persistent bloating, early satiety, pelvic pain; Red Flag: ascites, abdominal mass
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: CA-125; Pelvic TVUS; RMI score (>200 = MDT referral); CT Abdomen/Pelvis; Staging Laparotomy + Debulking + Carboplatin/Paclitaxel

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Regular painful contractions with progressive cervical effacement and dilation >=5cm
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Uterine basal tone & oxytocin-driven rhythmic contractions advancing station & rotation
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Regular uterine contractions, bloody show, rupture of membranes; expected progress >=1cm / 2 hours
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: WHO Labour Care Guide / Partograph monitoring; Fetal heart auscultation / IA; Vaginal exam q4h; Supportive care & pain relief

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Abnormal slow progress or arrest of labour; Etiology: 3 Ps (Power, Passenger, Passage)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD), malposition (occiput posterior), deflexion (brow/face), hypocontractile uterine power
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Protracted active phase, secondary arrest, severe moulding/caput (3+); Red Flag: Bandl's ring (impending rupture)
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Partograph action line crossed; If hypocontractile -> ARM + IV Oxytocin titration; If CPD/brow presentation -> Emergency C-Section

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Next-generation intrapartum monitoring tool replacing old partograph
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Focuses on respectful maternity care, active phase starting at 5cm, personalized alert triggers
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Alert line at <1cm/2h in active phase; systematically logs maternal/fetal well-being & labour progress
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Fetal heart rate q30m, contraction frequency/duration q30m, maternal BP q4h, urine output, cervical dilation q4h

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Continuous Electronic Fetal Monitoring using cardiotocography during high-risk labour
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Assesses fetal autonomic nervous system, brainstem perfusion, and oxygenation under contraction stress
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Normal baseline 110-160 bpm, variability 5-25 bpm, accelerations present; Pathological: late/repetitive variable decelerations
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: DR C BAVO system; Pathological CTG -> Fetal Scalp Blood Sampling (FSBS pH <7.20) or immediate Category 1 C-section

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Management of intrapartum delivery of twin B following successful birth of twin A
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Risk of malpresentation, cord prolapse, or placental abruption following decompression of twin A
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Abdominal palpation to confirm lie of Twin B; internal/external version if transverse; ARM once head engaged
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Continuous CTG Twin B; IV Oxytocin infusion ready; Ultrasound in delivery suite; Vacuum/forceps or ECV/internal podalic version

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Ascending polymicrobial upper genital tract infection; Chlamydia, N. gonorrhoeae, M. genitalium
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Endometrial, tubal, and peritoneal mucosal inflammation causing adhesions & tubo-ovarian abscess (TOA)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Bilateral lower abdominal pain, purulent cervical discharge, dyspareunia; Red Flags: chandelier sign, fever >38C, peritonitis
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Endocervical NAAT swabs; Pelvic TVUS; Outpatient: IM Ceftriaxone 1g + Oral Doxycycline 100mg BD + Metronidazole 400mg BD x14d

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Chronic severe itching of vulva/perineum; Lichen Sclerosus is autoimmune skin dermatosis
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Epidermal thinning, hyperkeratosis, dermal hyalinization, and loss of normal vulval architecture
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Intense vulval pruritus (worse at night), dyspareunia, porcelain-white figure-of-eight plaques around vulva/anus
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Vulval punch biopsy (if atypical/refractory); Ultra-potent topical corticosteroid (Clobetasol propionate 0.05%) for 3 months

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Non-pharmacological vs Pharmacological analgesia options during labour
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Central & peripheral pain pathway modulation during uterine contractions & perineal stretching
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Maternal request for analgesia during active labour phase
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Entonox (50% N2O / 50% O2); Parenteral Opioids (Pethidine / Remifentanil); Epidural analgesia (L3-L4 insertion - most effective)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: IOL: artificial initiation of labour; Augmentation: stimulation of established ineffective labour
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Cervical ripening via prostaglandins/mechanical methods followed by oxytocin-induced contractions
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Indications: post-term (41-42wks), pre-eclampsia, PPROM, SGA, maternal medical conditions
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Modified Bishop Score (>=8 favorable); Vaginal PGE2 (Propess/Prostin) or Mechanical balloon catheter -> ARM + IV Oxytocin

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Graphic representation of labour progress, maternal, and fetal condition over time
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Visual tracking of cervical dilation rate to detect early deviation from normal active phase progress
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Alert line reached = slow progress; Action line crossed = critical delay requiring intervention
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Plot cervical dilation from 4-5cm; Monitor contractions, fetal HR, moulding, caput, maternal BP/pulse, fluids/urine

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Late complication of severe undertreated PID; inflammatory mass involving tube and ovary
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Bacterial necrosis & purulent fluid collection within pelvic adnexa with tissue destruction
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Severe unilateral/bilateral pelvic pain, high fever, chills, adnexal mass, leukocytosis, elevated CRP
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Pelvic TVUS / CT pelvis (multilocular cystic adnexal mass); Inpatient IV Ceftriaxone + Doxycycline + Metronidazole; Surgical/percutaneous drainage

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Severe, disabling form of PMS with predominant affective and behavioral symptoms
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Cyclical neurosteroid & serotonin sensitivity fluctuations during luteal phase
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Severe mood swings, irritability, anxiety, depression resolving within a few days of menses onset
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Daily symptom diary over 2 cycles; First-line SSRIs (Sertraline / Fluoxetine) continuous or luteal-phase dosing; COCP (Yasmin)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome; most common cause of ovulatory dysfunction and secondary amenorrhea
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Hyperandrogenism, insulin resistance, and altered LH/FSH ratio (>2:1) causing anovulation
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Oligomenorrhea/amenorrhea, hirsutism, acne, central obesity, subfertility; bilateral polycystic ovaries on US
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Rotterdam Criteria (2 of 3: Oligo/anovulation, Hyperandrogenism, Polycystic ovaries >=20 follicles); Lifestyle/Weight loss + COCP / Letrozole
